To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the scintillation efficiency of NaI(Ti) crystals is linear between 3 Me V and 3 ke V and that it is not necessary to correct the measured scintillation efficiency for nonlinearity.

the observed nonlinear scintillation response is not an intrinsic feature of NaI(T1) but is caused by the effects of the radiation entrance surfaces and that the observed nonuniformities of the scintillation responses can be reduced by the application of an antireflection coating to the entrance surface.

the scintillation efficiency of NaI(Ti) is linear within 0.9% of a standard deviation in the energy range of 3 MeV to 3 keV and the nonlinearity observed in the energy range below 3 keV is most probably caused by effects occurring at radiation entrance surfaces of NaI(T1)-crystals.
